title: EDGE-LLM: Enabling Efficient Large Language Model Adaptation on Edge Devices via Unified Compression and Adaptive Layer Voting
problem: Efficient adaptation of large language models on edge devices suffers from high computation and memory overhead with existing tuning techniques. Edge devices require continuous, privacy-preserving adaptation and inference but lack the resources to support traditional LLM fine-tuning methods.
motivation: Enabling efficient LLM adaptation on edge devices is essential for privacy-preserving and real-time inference in distributed systems.
method: Edge-LLM introduces layer-wise unified compression (LUC) to reduce computation overhead through layer-wise pruning sparsity and quantization bit-width policies. An adaptive layer tuning and voting scheme reduces memory overhead by limiting backpropagation depth. A complementary hardware scheduling strategy handles irregular computation patterns from compression and adaptive tuning, improving real hardware efficiency.
key_novelty: The combination of layer-wise unified compression with adaptive layer voting and hardware-aware scheduling to enable efficient LLM adaptation on edge devices.
contributions: Layer-wise unified compression technique generating adaptive pruning sparsity and quantization policies per layer
Adaptive layer tuning and voting scheme that reduces backpropagation depth for memory efficiency
Hardware scheduling strategy to optimize irregular computation patterns from compression techniques
Achieves 2.92× speedup and 4× memory reduction while maintaining comparable task accuracy
primary_theme: Efficient LLM adaptation on edge devices
